subject: Sentra Labs - renewal readiness & usage / performance ROI review
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@sentralabs.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: usage, perf questions + ROI data request

Hi Rachel / Monica,

Renewal for Sentra is up next month and the finance team asked for a short packet summarizing our usage, latency/availability performance, and a concise ROI recap that justifies the proposed commit change. A couple of specific asks from Procurement and Engineering: 

- Token spend by environment (prod vs. staging) for Q2 and Q3 YTD
- Average generation latency p50/p95 under our current config and peak-week behavior
- Any observable inference regressions after model migration in June
- Suggested commit size to avoid throttles, and estimated unit-cost delta

I've attached the raw metrics export we pulled (sentra_prod_metrics_q2.csv). Can you confirm whether we should propose a 15% or 25% uplift to their committed capacity? Procurement would prefer a single recommended number plus a short justification.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform
Sentra Labs

P.S. Procurement copied: procurement@sentralabs.ai
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@sentralabs.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: usage, perf questions + ROI data request

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary and attached playbook.

TL;DR recommendation:
- Recommend a 20% commit increase (middle path): reduces peak throttling and keeps unit cost within 8-12% uplift vs current run rate when combined with optimized batching.
- Can offer a 3-month canary burst allowance to absorb unexpected spikes during product launches.

What I attached: sentra_renewal_playbook_v1.pdf and token_breakdown_q3.csv (cleaned view of token splits by env).

Highlights from our analysis:
- Q2 prod tokens: 1.9B; Q3 YTD (to Aug 1): 2.4B — 26% QoQ increase, most growth comes from the recommendations service.
- Latency (prod, gen path): p50=160ms, p95=420ms. During the June model switchover we observed a brief 10-15% p95 increase for 48 hours while warmups completed, then returned to baseline.
- Cost-saving levers already applied: prefix KV caching for recommendations and 4-token lookback truncation reduced infer-time by ~7% across calls. Further wins available via 8-bit quantized variant on the throughput tier.

Economic impact (back-of-envelope):
- If Sentra moves to +20% commit, unit token price effective change (after tiering) is estimated at +9% but expected to be offset by a 12% reduction in on-demand overage exposure and a 6% latency improvement from prewarmed cache in burst windows — net ROI: positive for product velocity (fewer throttles + predictable SLAs).

Next steps:
1) Monica to confirm recommended contract language and any discount structure.
2) If Procurement is comfortable, propose commit + 3-month canary and schedule a renewal call to sign the addendum.

Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@sentralabs.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: usage, perf questions + ROI data request

Thanks Rachel — great summary. A few contract/ops notes from my side: 

- Pricing: We can apply a graduated discount on the incremental commit tiers. For Sentra's current band and the proposed +20% uplift, a practical structure is: base price (current band) + 10% discount on incremental tokens up to +20%, then 5% beyond that.
- Term: Recommend 12-month term to lock the discount and preserve uplift economics; allow quarterly check-ins (operational cadence).
- Canary burst: We can formalize a 3-month burst credit pool (non-cumulative) to cover two major launches. We will need a short SLO appendix that defines acceptable latency degradation and mitigation steps.
- Procurement asks: Please confirm invoicing entity (Sentra Labs US vs EU) and PO lead contact; procurement@sentralabs.ai will handle.

Attachments & references: I will draft an addendum for the commit uplift and SLO appendix once procurement confirms invoicing.

Monica Patel
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@sentralabs.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: usage, perf questions + ROI data request

Looping in from Legal & Deals — quick confirmation:
- Approve the +20% commit recommendation with the pricing bands Monica proposed.
- We can extend a one-time 15% credit on the first month after renewals if Sentra signs within 21 days of the addendum delivery.
- Canary burst policy: Redwood will allow a defined burst credit pool for 90 days; if burst usage exceeds pool, overages billed at on-demand unless we agree an emergency uplift.

I'll prepare the addendum language and route for signatures once procurement confirms PO details. Rachel / Monica — can you confirm that the SLO appendix will require the p95 threshold and an operational contact for on-call incident escalation?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
